<p><span style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:107%;

EN-GB;mso-fareast-language:EN-US;mso-bidi-language:AR-SA">Insufficient
information has been provided for the Local Planning Authority to make a thorough
assessment with regards to trip generation, traffic and pedestrian safety, and
disturbance to the surrounding roads and therefore without further information
to suggest otherwise, the proposed development would be unacceptable due to its
highways, traffic generation, highway network and pedestrian safety impact
which is contrary to Policy 63 of Waltham Forests LP1 (2024), T2 and T4 of the
London Plan (2021).&nbsp;</span></p>

<p><span data-contrast="auto" xml:lang="EN-GB" lang="EN-GB" class="TextRun SCXW144569348 BCX0" style="-webkit-user-drag: none; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; margin: 0px; padding: 0px; user-select: text; font-size: 11pt; line-height: 18.3458px; font-family: Aptos, Aptos_EmbeddedFont, Aptos_MSFontService, sans-serif; font-variant-ligatures: none !important;">In principle, the accessibility and ability for National Grid to maintain/repair and to have access to the power cables, while guaranteeing power supply is a material planning consideration and therefore, it is concluded that development on the site is unacceptable in principle as would impede the ability to have access to the power cables. Furthermore, due to the nature of the use and with a lack of regard, or information about safety and maintenance to the cables, as such it would be contrary to Policies 6 (Ensuring Good Growth) and Policy 70 (utilities and infrastructure) of LP1 (2024), London Plan policies GG6 Increasing Efficiency and Resilience and D11 Safety, Security and Resilience which all seek to ensure that developments retain and protect infrastructure and for developments to have an acceptable impact.</span><span class="EOP SCXW144569348 BCX0" data-ccp-props="{}" style="-webkit-user-drag: none; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; margin: 0px; padding: 0px; user-select: text; font-size: 11pt; line-height: 18.3458px; font-family: Aptos, Aptos_EmbeddedFont, Aptos_MSFontService, sans-serif;">&nbsp;</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:107%;
font-family:&quot;Aptos&quot;,sans-serif;mso-ascii-theme-font:minor-latin;mso-fareast-font-family:
Aptos;mso-fareast-theme-font:minor-latin;mso-hansi-theme-font:minor-latin;
mso-bidi-font-family:Arial;mso-bidi-theme-font:minor-bidi;mso-ansi-language:
EN-GB;mso-fareast-language:EN-US;mso-bidi-language:AR-SA">The proposed
development fails to have proper regard to the potential environmental impacts
of the development by way of drainage, noise and air pollution. &nbsp;This is due to the present surface water
drainage issues and use which would increase water flows onsite, the proposed loud
machinery onsite in close proximity to residential dwellings, and the use which
would increase vehicle presence on site, and the failure submit a sustainable
urban drainage assessment, a noise report, or a air quality assessment for
these matters. It is therefore not clear how the proposed use would properly
deal with these environmental considerations &nbsp;and the proposed development under current
information is considered to cause environmental harm to the immediate locality
which would not be not supported by Policies 50, 88 and 91 of Waltham Forests
LP1 (2024).&nbsp;</span></p>

description: Change of use of vacant land to a hand car wash and valeting centre (Sui Generis) including the construction of a single storey office building, installation of jet washers and associated insulated housing including repaving of Land Adjacent to 205 Wadham Road, E17.
ward: Hale End and Highams Park South
